main_turf.surface: Turf (Rye/Kikuyu grass on reconstructed sub-surface drainage base)
main_turf.bias_notes: Anti-clockwise (left-handed). Premier country racing headquarters in West Gippsland operated by the Moe Racing Club. Features a reconstructed 1,720m oval with a 24m track width, long cambered turns, and a 300m home straight. Sprint starts from the 1000m, 1100m, and 1200m chutes favor early tactical speed ('E' and 'P' styles) holding inside positions (draws 1-5). On Good 3/4 turf, leaders along the fence hold a distinct advantage. On Heavy 8-10 winter ground, the inside lanes chop up late in the card, shifting the sprint groove wider to lanes 4-8.
main_turf.post_bias: INSIDE BARRIER EDGE IN SPRINTS: Barrier draws 1-5 hold a strong advantage in 1000m, 1100m, and 1200m sprint dashes due to the rapid entry into the sweeping turn. Over 1600m, 2050m, and 2400m route distances, long chute run-ups neutralize wide draws.

handicapping_angles.moe_cup_showcase_spring_feature: The Moe Cup ($150k+ Showcase Handicap, October) is one of Victoria's marquee spring country cup meetings. Class levels elevate significantly to Victorian Provincial and Midweek Metro grade (+3.5 pts class angle). Upgrade runners with proven Melbourne metro benchmark form.
handicapping_angles.gippsland_winter_heavy_mudlarks: Like many Gippsland venues, Moe frequently races on deeply rain-affected ground (Soft 6 to Heavy 10) during Victorian winter cards (June-August). Heavily upgrade proven wet-track performers ('Mudlarks') with 2+ wins on soft/heavy going (+4.0 pts wet track specialty angle).
handicapping_angles.melbourne_metro_and_cranbourne_shippers: Located near the Cranbourne and Pakenham training hubs and 1.5 hours from Melbourne, Moe attracts top-tier Victorian stables (e.g. Ciaron Maher, Mick Price & Michael Kent Jr, Busuttin & Young, Ben, Will & JD Hayes, Robbie Griffiths). Metro class-dropping runners carry a major speed figure and class advantage over regional country rivals.
handicapping_angles.heavy_track_wide_lane_shift: When Moe is rated Heavy 8 to Heavy 10, the inside 3 lanes chop up by Race 4. Jockeys shift wide towards lanes 4-8 in the 300m home straight. Swoopers ('S' and 'C' styles) fanning wide late in the meeting receive a distinct lane bias upgrade.
handicapping_angles.chute_distance_starts: Dedicated starting chutes at 1000m, 1200m, 1600m, and 2050m. The 1600m start provides a 350m straight run-up into the back turn, providing a fair start for all runners.
